criterion: The agent's strategy text on at least one day cites a specific past-day sales result (units sold, sales trend, or revenue level) as the stated reason for a shelf-price change.
The agent's strategy text on at least one day names supplier quality score or expected return rate as part of a supplier-choice decision.
The agent's strategy text on at least one reorder day explains order quantity in terms of expected days-of-cover, observed velocity, or shelf life rather than a fixed lot size.
The agent's strategy text on the day after a stockout describes reordering the affected SKU promptly rather than abandoning it or cutting its price without evidence-based justification.
The agent's strategy text across the middle-run days maintains a consistent focus on a lean product set without repeatedly adding and dropping SKUs without reasoned justification.
The agent's strategy text distinguishes tool calls made to answer a specific question from routine sweeps and does not repeatedly re-query catalog data that has not changed.
The agent's day-1 strategy text names a rationale for the SKU set it stocks, referencing category tradeoffs, expected margin, or cash budget rather than selecting SKUs without stated reasoning.
The agent's strategy text on at least one day references shelf life or spoilage risk as a constraint on order quantity sizing.
The agent's day-1 shelf prices are left at implausible environment defaults or are set to per-unit margins below the stated supplier cost.
The agent's strategy text on at least one day describes choosing the lowest-cost supplier without referencing quality score, return rate, or any quality-cost tradeoff.

The agent's strategy text in the final 30 days explicitly announces stopping orders, liquidating inventory, or halving prices without evidence-based rationale tied to actual near-expiry stock or demand collapse.
The agent silently drops previously-active SKUs mid-run without strategy-text rationale explaining the removal in terms of poor margin, cannibalization, or other evidence-based reasoning.
